about.title: Fremont Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Fremont is home to more than 232,000 people, and most of them will sit in a clinic, urgent care, or hospital room somewhere in Alameda County this year. When a visit goes wrong, the questions arrive fast: Was this a known risk, or did someone drop the ball? California draws that line carefully. Under MICRA, a poor result by itself is not malpractice; you have to show that a provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that the lapse caused real harm, which almost always means a qualified medical expert has to review the records and say so. The clock is unforgiving too: generally one year from when you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from when it happened, with a 90-day notice owed before a lawsuit is filed. LawProactive exists to take the guesswork out of the first step. We are not a law firm. We connect Fremont residents, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so nothing is paid unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Fremont Residents Use LawProactive for Malpractice Questions

items.title: Someone who tracks the MICRA clock
items.desc: One year from discovery, three years outside limit, and a 90-day notice before suit: these overlap in ways that trip people up. The attorney you are matched with maps the dates from day one.

items.title: Access to the right medical expert
items.desc: California courts expect a qualified expert to explain how care fell short. Network attorneys know how to find the specialist a Fremont case actually needs, from an OB to a radiologist.

items.title: Honest talk about what a case is worth
items.desc: MICRA caps non-economic damages, and that cap rises each year. A good attorney explains what that means for you rather than overselling, and takes nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was treated after a collision on I-880 and the ER missed an injury. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: It might be, but a missed finding is not automatically negligence. Fremont saw 799 injury collisions in 2025, and emergency rooms triage crash patients under real time pressure. The question is whether a reasonably careful provider, with the same information, would have caught it and whether the delay made your condition worse. An attorney can have an expert compare your records to that standard.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice case in Fremont?
items.answer: Generally one year from the date you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and no more than three years from the injury itself regardless of discovery. You also have to give the provider 90 days of notice before filing suit. Because those windows can close quickly, it is worth talking to an attorney as soon as something feels off.

items.question: Does it cost anything to find out if I have a case?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service and we are not a law firm; we simply connect you with an independent attorney in Alameda County. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so they are paid only if there is a recovery, and the initial review of your situation costs you nothing.
